answer: In the primary proportional-odds ordinal logistic model (subject-level max AESEV for AEPT=='COVID-19', categories 1-4; n=148 infected subjects: 76 BCG / 72 placebo), the common BCG odds ratio for a HIGHER COVID-19 severity category is 1.36 (95% CI 0.24-7.61) at the covariate reference (mh_count=0, patients_seen=1-50); at covariate medians (mh_count=1, patients_seen=1) it is 0.94 (0.11-7.71) and at means 0.82 (0.08-8.90). Equivalently, exp(beta_BCG)=0.74 (SE 0.88) is the common OR of being in the lower-or-equal category. The requested interaction terms are not significant: BCG:patients_seen OR 0.70 (0.24-2.09) and BCG:mh_count OR 0.98 (0.57-1.69). The CI is very wide and includes 1: there is no statistically detectable effect of BCG on severity in this data (crude OR for severity>=3 is 3.89, driven by 11/76 BCG vs 3/72 placebo subjects). Proportional odds is NOT formally rejected (Brant chi2=8.02, df=10, p=0.63), but the assumption is fragile: the top cutpoint is quasi-separated (only 14 subjects at severity>=3), per-cutpoint BCG ORs range from ~0.7 to >10, and a partial-odds model reaches a boundary MLE that fits the sparse top category far better (delta-negll=48), so the standard LRT is invalid. Sensitivities keep the answer near null: MH count = all MH rows -> BCG OR 1.07 at medians (near-singular fit, CI ~0-2.5e6); all MHTERM rows -> 0.93 (near-singular); expect_interact instead of patients_seen -> 1.21 (0.09-15.8) with a BCG:expect_interact OR of 3.05 (0.78-11.9); imputing missing severity as category 1 (n=189) -> 0.86 (0.18-4.14); midpoint coding of patients_seen -> 0.93 (0.26-3.34). Headline: OR ~1.4 (0.2-7.6) at reference, ~0.9 (0.1-7.7) at medians; effect indistinguishable from null.
